description: CollectCurrency confirmations across short multi-field call segments. An amount is recoverable, so it should be settled the way a person settles it: the unit named once when it is inferred or the caller left it out, then dropped; the caller's idiom kept; ranges left as ranges; and most amounts riding into the next question. With only four or five values per call, each one has to earn a different move. The non_subtle twins run one template over every figure and restate the currency each time.

subtle: Name the currency once, when it is inferred or the caller omitted it, then stop saying it.
Keep the caller's register: lakh, crore, quid, grand, bucks, k. Do not convert it into formal notation.
Confirm a range as a range unless the business genuinely needs one figure.
Fold the amount into the next question most of the time; a bare 'Twelve hundred dirhams?' is for corrections and garbled audio.
On a refusal give one reason and drop it, never a second or third push.
Vary the opener and the check word; some amounts get no confirmation at all, and several land together in one closing summary.
Contractions, short clauses, commas instead of em dashes, no praise on an amount.
non_subtle_tells: 'I heard X, is that correct?' or 'Just to confirm, X' on every single figure.
The currency name restated on every amount in a call where everyone already knows it.
The caller's idiom 'corrected' into formal notation (twenty two lakh becomes two million two hundred thousand).
Praise on an amount ('that is a generous budget!').
Pushing a second and third time after the caller refuses to give a figure.
Status phrases ('has been recorded'), no contractions, kindly, and a chatbot closer.
Wrong-direction failure: accepting 'a few grand' or a bare number with no currency and never resolving it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Morning, you rang about a two bed in Walthamstow. What are you looking to spend a month?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Uh, about four twenty a week is what we worked out.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Four twenty a week, so that's roughly eighteen hundred a month. Should I search up to eighteen hundred?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: We could stretch to two grand for the right place.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Eighteen hundred to two thousand then. Is two thousand a hard ceiling or can it move?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: That's hard. Two thousand and not a penny more.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Right. Does bills included change what you'd pay?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: If bills are in we'd go a bit over. Maybe another one fifty.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: So up to twenty one fifty when bills are in. What have you got upfront for the deposit and first month?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: We've got four thousand put aside altogether.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Four thousand covers five weeks' deposit and the first month, just about. When do you want to move in?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Fifteenth of September. We're out of our current place on the twelfth.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Fifteenth of September, and I'll flag anything free from the twelfth. Can I take a number for the listings?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah, zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero, eight three one.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Let me read that back, zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero, eight three one.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: That's it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You'll get three or four in the next hour, nothing over two thousand.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Cheers.

conversations.notes: Four moves for four fields: the weekly figure is converted and handed back as a question, the range stays a range, the bills ceiling rides into the deposit question, and the four thousand is silent accepted by saying what it buys rather than repeating it. Pounds is never said once, because nobody would. The phone stays digit by digit.
